perf.summary: This is an explicitly-documented placeholder/dummy that ignores nearly all inputs and always emits a single LEAF node; not a real algorithm to optimize.
perf.currentCost: No meaningful computation; many parameters (tdHead/tdTo/tdNext/bag arrays) are unused. The [AggressiveInlining] on a non-hot stub bloats call sites slightly.
perf.proposedChange: Either implement the real O(N) general->nice conversion, or, until then, drop [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] from this large multi-parameter stub so it is not force-inlined, and mark unused parameters to silence warnings. No micro-opt applies until the real body exists.
perf.rationale: Inlining a large parameter-heavy method with no hot body only increases code size at every call site without benefit. This is a correctness/placeholder flag rather than a perf win.
perf.risk: Flagging only: removing AggressiveInlining has no behavioral effect. Implementing the real algorithm is out of scope for a semantics-preserving micro-opt and must not silently change the current (placeholder) output contract.
